transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-01
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Aisha Noor (Redwood CSM); Sara Gomez (Nimbus Head of ML), Tom Reed (Eng Manager), Priya Singh (Data Privacy), Evan Cole (NLP Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Weekly quality sync. Focus on eval regressions and guardrail tuning. Action items assigned.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Lena): hey everyone thanks for jumping on, quick agenda: go over the latest eval numbers, flag regressions from the last deploy, and agree next steps. Marcus will run through the details.
00:24 Speaker 2 (Marcus): cool yep uh so we ran the 5k prompt set overnight against the current served model v1.3, and the collapsed score for safety/regression is roughly 87% pass rate, down from 92 in the baseline. most of the drop is in the medical Q&A subset where we see hallucinations and dosage rounding.
00:47 Speaker 3 (Sara): sorry can you repeat that, 87% pass across the whole set or just safety?
00:55 Marcus: whole set; safety-only is 82%. baseline was 91/89 respectively. the biggest buckets are hallucination on drug interactions, and a smaller bucket of format errors where the model omits units.
01:14 Tom: is this from hosted infra or the dedicated instance we spun up?
01:19 Marcus: these are hosted API runs (our staging hosted pool) — we haven't yet run the dedicated GPU pool for this eval, so cost/latency numbers are separate.
01:31 Sara: do we have examples of the hallucinations? can we see a few?
01:36 Marcus: yes I'll pull a couple. example: prompt asked "Recommended statin dosage for a 68-year-old with x condition" and model responded with a specific mg suggestion then added an unsupported drug interaction. that's the kind of assertive error we flagged.
01:58 Evan: hmm some of those prompts are borderline — did you include the context that this is for product guidance not clinical? we should label which are "medical advice" vs "documentation lookup".
02:12 Marcus: good call, our labeling pipeline currently has a mixed tag. Evan if you can upload clearer labels we can slice the eval by those tags.
02:24 Evan: will do.
02:28 Priya: just flagging from privacy standpoint, when we share prompts they may include PHI. we need to scrub or sign NDA. what's your current retention policy on hosted logs?
02:40 Lena: Redwood hosted retains transcripts 30 days by default for trial accounts; we can restrict or enable redaction for pilot accounts and for Private deployments we can disable retention entirely and integrate customer KMS.
02:55 Priya: okay let's get that in writing, I'll need SOC2 evidence too.
03:03 Lena: yes I'll share the security deck and our SOC2 report link after the call.
03:10 Marcus: back to evals — we also ran a classifier guardrail (a toxicity/medical-safety classifier) that filtered outputs post-hoc; it recovered about 6% of the failing cases but introduced false positives in clinical style prompts where the model used clinical language but was accurate.
03:34 Sara: what's the precision/recall there?
03:38 Marcus: roughly precision 0.91 recall 0.58 on the medical safety holdout; we tuned threshold to favor precision which reduces false rejections but misses edge hallucinations.
03:49 Tom: can we chain the guardrail with a clarifying prompt instead of outright blocking? like 'I may not have complete info, consult your physician'??
03:58 Marcus: yep that's an approach — we support safety fallback templates and you can route to a lower-confidence flow that inserts a disclaimers and requires human review. that reduces UX friction but increases operational overhead.
04:18 Sara: UX is super important for clinicians; too many disclaimers may break trust. we prefer fewer blocks and more context disclaimers when low confidence.
04:29 Marcus: noted. we can tune the classifier thresholds and change the fallback messaging.
04:34 Evan: any chance of running these tests on Redwood Dedicated? curious about latency on long context docs and cost per 1k tokens.
04:42 Marcus: yes we planned to run that — estimated delta: Dedicated with a 4x A100-style pool reduces 95th pct latency by ~40% and token cost by ~20% compared to bursty hosted pricing, but actual numbers depend on batching and quantization profile. we'll run a bench and share.
05:03 Tom: what's the KV cache story — can the same patient doc context be cached between related queries?
05:10 Marcus: we do prefix/KV caching for sessions; in Private you can persist tenant caches across instances depending on config; hosted keeps cache ephemeral per session for privacy unless you opt into longer lived caches. there's some mis-transcribe sometimes it's called 'kee-vee cache' in docs.
05:31 Sara: thanks. on the scoring spreadsheet we saw a lot of edge cases labeled 'ambiguous' — what's your recommended workflow?
05:38 Aisha (CSM): recommended is to surface ambiguous cases to a human labeler queue and after we get labels run a small reweighting on the eval. that should improve both precision and recall.
05:49 Evan: I'll take ownership of ambiguous labeling with my team.
05:53 Marcus: great — for the next run we propose adding a second guardrail classifier trained on the ambiguous set; that usually recovers another 3-5% pass rate without harming precision.
06:07 Priya: timeline for retraining that classifier?
06:10 Marcus: if you upload the labeled ambiguous set by next Tuesday we can train and run results by Friday (i.e., 3 business days).
06:19 Evan: sounds good.
06:22 Sara: can we talk briefly about regression detection — we saw a spike after the last model patch; how do you surface model diffs automatically?
06:31 Marcus: we run nightly diff jobs comparing a canary to baseline over the canonical prompt set; diffs trigger alerts on metric drift (safety/format/semantic). we also surface a highlighted list of 20 worst regressions for manual review. seems like we missed some clinical cases last deploy due to label drift.
06:52 Tom: is there a way to pin a model version per route so production traffic isn't impacted?
06:57 Lena: yes you can pin routes to model versions and also do canary rollouts and automatic rollback on X% regression. that is in the rollout feature.
07:10 Sara: for reporting we want a csv export with per-prompt scores and example responses for each failing case. can you provide that?
07:18 Marcus: yes we'll attach the raw CSV and a dashboard link.
07:21 Tom: any known false negative classes we should preemptively test?
07:26 Marcus: drug-drug interaction paraphrases and implicit dosing (like 'double my dose' phrased colloquially) often slip through. also tables and units formatting occasionally get dropped.
07:41 Evan: on prompt engineering, we tried adding 'do not give medical advice' at the top and it helped but didn't eliminate confident hallucinations.
07:50 Marcus: right those guardrails help but don't replace classifier thresholds. combination works best.
07:56 Sara: do we have recommended templates for clinicians to reduce hallucination?
08:00 Marcus: yes we have clinician template examples in the playbook, I'll share the link. it's called 'Clinical Prompt Kit' but sometimes transcribed as 'clinic prompt kit'.
08:11 Priya: on compliance, to consider private deployment we need: on-prem option, KMS integration, audit logs retention control, and support for customer-managed VPC. can Redwood satisfy those?
08:24 Lena: yes. Private deployments support customer KMS/HSM, full audit logs with configurable retention, and VPC-only control plane. we'll include the private deployment spec in the follow-up.
08:37 Sara: performance tradeoffs — any rough cost numbers for private vs dedicated vs hosted for our 50 qps pilot?
08:44 Marcus: preliminary estimate: hosted burst pricing likely higher per-token; dedicated reserved capacity with batching reduces unit cost 15-25%; private on-prem depends on infra amortization but can be lowest if you already have GPUs and ops. we'll give a more precise estimate after we run the bench.
09:02 Tom: re: bench — please include a long-document scenario (10k token patient note) as that's our common worst case.
09:10 Marcus: noted, we'll include that.
09:13 Sara: ok let's recap next steps.
09:17 Lena: recap: Redwood to share scoring dashboard + raw CSV, security docs and SOC2 link; Marcus to rerun eval with updated guardrail and bench dedicated pool; Nimbus to upload 1k more prompts and label ambiguous cases; schedule security deep-dive.
09:36 Sara: thanks all. any other questions?
09:40 Priya: none from me.
09:42 Evan: none.
09:43 Lena: great we'll follow up with notes and links. talk soon.
09:48 End of call
